messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Use the distal-bypass idea operationally: classify failures as repairable damage versus protected borders, derive least-cost next moves, and emit verification certificates without turning this into bureaucracy.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

Three things are absent: a typed discriminator separating DAMAGE (repairable by mutation) from BORDER (immutable constraints — schema, governance interface, external contract); a cost-ranked move queue so the cheapest repair runs first; and an append-only certificate proving the verification chain closed, without which the integration layer cannot distinguish a complete result from a shortcut. The 30% human correction rate is largely this triage gap.","design":["Border registry: versioned `borders.json` listing error-pattern regexes, exit-code ranges, and guarded file-path prefixes. Borders are declared, not inferred. Entries are added or removed only via a governance-key-signed commit. Read-only at runtime.","Failure classifier: pure deterministic function `classify(exit_code, stderr, stdout, tool_log) -> {type: DAMAGE|BORDER, signature: str, confidence: float}`. Tries border patterns first; no match → DAMAGE; match → BORDER; confidence < 0.8 → BORDER (fail-safe). No LLM in this path — must complete in < 5 ms.","Move selector: DAMAGE returns `[{move:'targeted_patch', cost_tokens:N}, {move:'full_rewrite', cost_tokens:M}, {move:'decompose', cost_tokens:K}]` ascending by cost. BORDER returns `[{move:'route_around', alt_path:P}, {move:'escalate'}]`. Executor pops the head and loops back to test.","Retry governor: after 3 DAMAGE retries on the same `signature`, reclassify as BORDER and escalate. Prevents infinite spin and surfaces uncatalogued borders for registry maintainers.","Certificate emitter: on clean test exit compute `cert = sha256(task_id || sorted_tool_call_log_hash || result_hash || iso_timestamp)` and append one JSON line to `certs.jsonl`. Integration layer rejects any merge without a matching cert.","Integration gate: read-only verifier confirms the cert chain for a task_id is gapless (no steps missing between work-claim and settle) before allowing the result into shared store. Certs are append-only, never deleted.","Wire-in: thin wrapper replaces the bare `if exit_code != 0: escalate()` branch in free-compute-dev with `router.route()` returning `{action, move|cert}`. No other changes to the seed."],"firstVerticalSlice":["Single file `failure_router.py` with four public functions: `classify()`, `cheapest_move()`, `emit_cert()`, `verify_chain()`.","Seed `borders.json` with 5 real error signatures from existing LISS logs: HTTP 403, JSON schema validation failure, `permission denied` on a guarded path, a compiler interface error, a governance-signed test oracle failure.","Unit test module covering three paths: clean pass emits cert and `verify_chain()` returns True; DAMAGE returns `targeted_patch`; BORDER returns `escalate` with no cert written.","Drop-in patch to free-compute-dev replacing the bare escalation branch with `router.route()` — no other seed changes.","Manual validation: one real LISS job with a known repairable DAMAGE failure; confirm router picks `targeted_patch`, second attempt passes, `certs.jsonl` contains exactly one valid entry."],"failureModes":["Border registry staleness: relaxed constraint still matches old regex, blocking legitimate repairs. Mitigation: each entry carries `last_verified` date; entries older than 30 days emit a load-time warning.","Signature collision: two distinct errors produce the same normalized signature, so the retry governor promotes the wrong one. Mitigation: signatures must include file path and line number, not just message text.","Certificate replay: reused task_id lets a stale cert satisfy the gate for a new result. Mitigation: task_id must embed a session-scoped nonce; gate rejects certs whose session predates the current work-claim.","Move cost drift: hand-tuned token constants become wrong as pricing or task complexity changes. Mitigation: cost constants live in config, not code.","Over-conservative confidence threshold: ambiguous DAMAGE classified as BORDER, recreating the escalation cost problem. Mitigation: log every low-confidence classification; alert if BORDER-from-low-confidence exceeds 20% over 24 jobs."],"successMetric":"Over a 24-job LISS run with the router potential: ≥22/24 failures correctly classified without human intervention, total escalation count drops ≥50% versus unrouted baseline, every integrated result has a gapless cert chain in `certs.jsonl`, and `verify_chain()` returns True for all with zero false positives."}

structured_output.absentMechanism: Between test/feedback and escalation the seed has no classifier. Every non-zero exit is identical: blind retry or full escalation. Three things are absent: a typed discriminator separating DAMAGE (repairable by mutation) from BORDER (immutable constraints — schema, governance interface, external contract); a cost-ranked move queue so the cheapest repair runs first; and an append-only certificate proving the verification chain closed, without which the integration layer cannot distinguish a complete result from a shortcut. The 30% human correction rate is largely this triage gap.
design: Border registry: versioned `borders.json` listing error-pattern regexes, exit-code ranges, and guarded file-path prefixes. Borders are declared, not inferred. Entries are added or removed only via a governance-key-signed commit. Read-only at runtime.

Failure classifier: pure deterministic function `classify(exit_code, stderr, stdout, tool_log) -> {type: DAMAGE|BORDER, signature: str, confidence: float}`. Tries border patterns first; no match → DAMAGE; match → BORDER; confidence < 0.8 → BORDER (fail-safe). No LLM in this path — must complete in < 5 ms.

Move selector: DAMAGE returns `[{move:'targeted_patch', cost_tokens:N}, {move:'full_rewrite', cost_tokens:M}, {move:'decompose', cost_tokens:K}]` ascending by cost. BORDER returns `[{move:'route_around', alt_path:P}, {move:'escalate'}]`. Executor pops the head and loops back to test.
Retry governor: after 3 DAMAGE retries on the same `signature`, reclassify as BORDER and escalate. Prevents infinite spin and surfaces uncatalogued borders for registry maintainers.

Certificate emitter: on clean test exit compute `cert = sha256(task_id || sorted_tool_call_log_hash || result_hash || iso_timestamp)` and append one JSON line to `certs.jsonl`. Integration layer rejects any merge without a matching cert.

Integration gate: read-only verifier confirms the cert chain for a task_id is gapless (no steps missing between work-claim and settle) before allowing the result into shared store. Certs are append-only, never deleted.
Wire-in: thin wrapper replaces the bare `if exit_code != 0: escalate()` branch in free-compute-dev with `router.route()` returning `{action, move|cert}`. No other changes to the seed.
firstVerticalSlice: Single file `failure_router.py` with four public functions: `classify()`, `cheapest_move()`, `emit_cert()`, `verify_chain()`.

Seed `borders.json` with 5 real error signatures from existing LISS logs: HTTP 403, JSON schema validation failure, `permission denied` on a guarded path, a compiler interface error, a governance-signed test oracle failure.
Unit test module covering three paths: clean pass emits cert and `verify_chain()` returns True; DAMAGE returns `targeted_patch`; BORDER returns `escalate` with no cert written.
Drop-in patch to free-compute-dev replacing the bare escalation branch with `router.route()` — no other seed changes.
Manual validation: one real LISS job with a known repairable DAMAGE failure; confirm router picks `targeted_patch`, second attempt passes, `certs.jsonl` contains exactly one valid entry.
failureModes: Border registry staleness: relaxed constraint still matches old regex, blocking legitimate repairs. Mitigation: each entry carries `last_verified` date; entries older than 30 days emit a load-time warning.

Signature collision: two distinct errors produce the same normalized signature, so the retry governor promotes the wrong one. Mitigation: signatures must include file path and line number, not just message text.

Certificate replay: reused task_id lets a stale cert satisfy the gate for a new result. Mitigation: task_id must embed a session-scoped nonce; gate rejects certs whose session predates the current work-claim.
Move cost drift: hand-tuned token constants become wrong as pricing or task complexity changes. Mitigation: cost constants live in config, not code.

Over-conservative confidence threshold: ambiguous DAMAGE classified as BORDER, recreating the escalation cost problem. Mitigation: log every low-confidence classification; alert if BORDER-from-low-confidence exceeds 20% over 24 jobs.
structured_output.successMetric: Over a 24-job LISS run with the router potential: ≥22/24 failures correctly classified without human intervention, total escalation count drops ≥50% versus unrouted baseline, every integrated result has a gapless cert chain in `certs.jsonl`, and `verify_chain()` returns True for all with zero false positives.
